disposition_reason: The results text prints city-level cadmium concentrations in marketed milk; lead is figure-only.

study.market: commercially available milk supply chain, Lahore, Faisalabad and Jhang
study.method: wet digestion (1 mL milk, nitric then perchloric acid), graphite furnace AAS (PerkinElmer AAnalyst 800); results expressed in ng/L

findings.integrity_flag: printed unit ng/L conflicts with Figure 2 axis (ug/L) and with the claim that all samples exceed the 2.6 ug/kg cadmium limit
findings.notes: Per-litre result kept unconverted (value_ugkg null). Described as the city's highest contamination across months; the statistic behind it (monthly mean or single sample) is not stated. 60 samples per city per year.

controls.outcome: cadmium fell from 0.034 to 0.020 ng/L between March and July; higher in winter (figure for monthly values)

unresolved: Lead results are shown only in Figure 3 (axis labelled mg/L, about 0.04-0.06); the body text prints no lead value. The abstract gives Lahore lead 0.062 ng/L, which is not recorded because it is not printed in the results.

Unit conflict: text and methods say ng/L, Figure 2 axis says ug/L and Figure 3 axis says mg/L; the paper also states all samples exceed limits of 2.6 ug/kg cadmium and 20 ug/kg lead, which only fits ug/L or higher. Values kept as printed.
Monthly cadmium values by city are figure-only (Figure 2): highest in winter/flush months, lowest in June/July.
The masthead prints "JAN - JUN 2020" while the issue is Volume 4, Issue 2 (July-Sep 2023), published 30 September 2023.
Aflatoxin M1 results (Tables 1-4) are not metal findings.
